neighbours.label: bat-and-ball sports play-by-play (baseball, cricket): tokens leading into fielding/pitching terms
fire: The visitors won the toss and chose to bowl first on a damp morning pitch.
On the very next delivery the opener edged it straight to the wicket keeper.
The left-hander struck out the side with a sharp curveball in the seventh inning.
With two outs, the shortstop fielded the grounder cleanly and threw to first.
He worked the count full before lining the next pitch into right field.
The spinner kept the batsmen quiet with tight control around off stump.
Our catcher called for a slider, and the runner took off for second base.
The captain set an attacking field with three slips and a gully.
quiet: The visitors won the coin toss and chose to kick off first on a damp morning.
On the very next possession the striker headed it straight to the goalkeeper.
The point guard hit a sharp crossover and scored in the third quarter.
With two seconds left, the center grabbed the rebound and passed to the wing.
He worked the defense patiently before slotting the next shot into the net.
The midfielder kept the opponents quiet with tight marking around the box.
Our quarterback called for a screen, and the receiver took off downfield.
The coach set an attacking formation with three forwards and a winger.

notes: card: top examples are cricket toss/field, baseball pitch descriptions; + pole is runs/home runs counts
